prompt: Was the founder of the bank that was established 42 years before the National Banking Act was expanded to include the Territory of Hawai'i still alive when it acquired Pioneer Federal Savings Bank?
answer: No. The bank’s predecessor was established in **1858 by Charles Reed Bishop**, 42 years before U.S. national banking legislation was extended to the Territory of Hawaiʻi in 1900. Bishop died on **June 7, 1915**; First Hawaiian acquired Pioneer Federal Savings Bank on **August 6, 1993**. Thus, he had been dead for about **78 years** at the time of the acquisition.
